## Introduction
Terrorism is a major global security concern that affects countries, governments, and civilian populations. Understanding historical patterns in terrorist attacks can help identify geographic trends, common attack methods, and the severity of incidents across different regions.

For this project, I will analyze the Global Terrorism Database, which contains information about terrorist incidents worldwide from 1970 to 2017. I will examine how the frequency of attacks has changed over time, which countries have experienced the most incidents, which attack types have resulted in the most fatalities, and how terrorist activity varies across geographic regions. I will also investigate the relationship between fatalities and injuries.

The goal of this analysis is to better understand historical patterns in terrorism and identify trends that may be useful for national security research and policy analysis.

## Loading in Packages
```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
```

## Loading in Data
```{python}
data = pd.read_csv(
    "C:/Users/SheaD/Wrangling/globalterrorism_data.csv",
    encoding="latin1",
    low_memory=False
)

data.head()
data.tail()
data.shape
data.dtypes
data.describe(include='all')
data.isnull().sum()
```

The dataset contains 181,691 observations and 135 variables. Each observation represents a recorded terrorist incident, while the variables describe characteristics such as the location, year, attack type, casualties, and group responsible.

## Cleaning the Data
```{python}
columns = [
    'iyear',
    'country_txt',
    'region_txt',
    'attacktype1_txt',
    'targtype1_txt',
    'weaptype1_txt',
    'nkill',
    'nwound',
    'gname',
    'success'
]

data = data[columns].copy()

data = data.rename(columns={
    'iyear': 'year',
    'country_txt': 'country',
    'region_txt': 'region',
    'attacktype1_txt': 'attack_type',
    'targtype1_txt': 'target_type',
    'weaptype1_txt': 'weapon_type',
    'nkill': 'fatalities',
    'nwound': 'injuries',
    'gname': 'group_name'
})

data['fatalities'] = pd.to_numeric(
    data['fatalities'], errors='coerce'
)

data['injuries'] = pd.to_numeric(
    data['injuries'], errors='coerce'
)

data.isnull().sum()

data.head()
```

I wrote this code to prepare the dataset for answering my five research questions. First, I selected ten variables that were most relevant to my analysis and renamed several columns to make them easier to understand and work with. I also converted the fatalities and injuries columns to numeric values to ensure they could be used in calculations and visualizations.

After examining missing values, I found that some incidents did not have recorded fatality or injury counts. Rather than removing all of these observations, I decided to handle missing values separately for questions involving casualties. This allows me to preserve as much information as possible when analyzing the frequency and geographic distribution of terrorist attacks.

## Question 1: How has the number of terrorist attacks changed over time? 
```{python}
yearly_attacks = data.groupby('year').size()

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

plt.plot(yearly_attacks.index, yearly_attacks.values,
         color='darkred', marker='o')

plt.title('Global Terrorist Attacks Over Time (1970–2017)')
plt.xlabel('Year')
plt.ylabel('Number of Terrorist Attacks')

plt.grid(True)

plt.show()

print(yearly_attacks)
```

This code was used to examine how the number of recorded terrorist attacks changed between 1970 and 2017. I grouped the dataset by year and counted the number of incidents occurring annually. I then created a line chart to visualize historical trends and highlighted the year with the highest number of attacks.

The results show that recorded terrorist attacks increased significantly over the period, particularly after 2011. The highest number of incidents occurred in 2014, with 16,903 recorded attacks. Following this peak, the number of attacks declined to 10,900 in 2017. These findings suggest that terrorist activity was not consistent over time, with certain periods experiencing substantial increases in recorded incidents. Changes in reporting and database coverage may also affect the observed trends.

## Question 2: Which countries experienced the highest number of terrorist attacks? 
```{python}
country_attacks = data.groupby('country').size()

top_countries = country_attacks.sort_values(ascending=False).head(10)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

plt.barh(top_countries.index, top_countries.values, color='red')

plt.title('Top 10 Countries with the Most Terrorist Attacks')
plt.xlabel('Number of Terrorist Attacks')
plt.ylabel('Country')

plt.show()

print(top_countries)
```

This code was used to identify the ten countries that experienced the highest number of recorded terrorist attacks. I grouped the dataset by country and counted the total number of incidents associated with each country. I then sorted the results and created a horizontal bar chart to compare the countries.

The results show that Iraq experienced the highest number of recorded terrorist attacks, with 24,636 incidents, followed by Pakistan with 14,368 and Afghanistan with 12,731. India and Colombia also ranked among the countries with the most incidents. These findings indicate that terrorist activity has been concentrated in certain countries, particularly those that have experienced prolonged political instability or armed conflict. However, these are cumulative counts over the study period rather than population-adjusted rates.

## Question 3: Which types of terrorist attacks resulted in the highest average number of fatalities? 
```{python}
fatality_data = data.dropna(subset=['fatalities'])

attack_fatalities = fatality_data.groupby('attack_type')['fatalities'].mean()

attack_fatalities = attack_fatalities.sort_values(ascending=False)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

plt.barh(attack_fatalities.index, attack_fatalities.values, color='blue')

plt.title('Average Fatalities per Incident by Attack Type')
plt.xlabel('Average Number of Fatalities')
plt.ylabel('Attack Type')

plt.gca().invert_yaxis()

plt.show()

print(attack_fatalities)
```

This code was used to compare the average number of fatalities associated with different types of terrorist attacks. I removed observations with missing fatality counts, grouped the remaining data by attack type, and calculated the average number of fatalities per incident. I then created a horizontal bar chart to compare the severity of different attack methods.

The results show that hijackings had the highest average number of fatalities, with approximately 6.14 deaths per incident. Hostage-taking involving barricade situations had the second-highest average, with approximately 4.99 fatalities. Armed assaults averaged approximately 3.97 fatalities per incident, while facility and infrastructure attacks had the lowest average at approximately 0.37. These findings suggest that certain types of attacks tend to result in more fatalities per incident than others. However, averages can be influenced by unusually severe incidents, and the analysis excludes observations with unknown fatality counts.

## Question 4: How have terrorist attack patterns differed across geographic regions over time? 
For this question, I chose a heatmap because it allows me to compare terrorist activity across multiple regions and years in one visualization. Darker colors will represent years and regions with higher numbers of recorded attacks.
```{python}
recent_data = data[data['year'] >= 2000]

region_year = recent_data.groupby(['region', 'year']).size()

heatmap_data = region_year.unstack(fill_value=0)

plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))

sns.heatmap(heatmap_data, cmap='Reds')

plt.title('Global Terrorist Attacks by Region and Year (2000–2017)')
plt.xlabel('Year')
plt.ylabel('Region')

plt.show()

print(heatmap_data)
```

This code was used to examine how the number of terrorist attacks differed across geographic regions between 2000 and 2017. I filtered the dataset to focus on more recent historical incidents, grouped the data by region and year, and counted the number of attacks. I then used pivot_table() to reorganize the data into a format suitable for a heatmap, where each row represents a geographic region and each column represents a year.

The heatmap uses lighter colors to represent fewer attacks and darker red colors to represent higher numbers of attacks. The results show that the Middle East and North Africa and South Asia experienced particularly high concentrations of terrorist activity, especially after 2011. The Middle East and North Africa recorded its highest number of attacks in 2014, with 6,939 incidents. These findings demonstrate that terrorist activity has varied considerably across regions and time, with certain areas experiencing significant increases in recorded incidents.

## Question 5: Is there a relationship between the number of fatalities and injuries in terrorist attacks? 
For this question, I chose a scatter plot with a regression line to determine whether incidents with more fatalities also tend to result in more injuries.
```{python}
casualty_data = data.dropna(subset=['fatalities', 'injuries'])

correlation = casualty_data['fatalities'].corr(casualty_data['injuries'])

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

plt.scatter(casualty_data['fatalities'],
            casualty_data['injuries'],
            color='red', alpha=0.3)

plt.title('Relationship Between Fatalities and Injuries')
plt.xlabel('Number of Fatalities')
plt.ylabel('Number of Injuries')

plt.show()

print('Correlation:', correlation)
```

This code was used to examine whether terrorist incidents resulting in more fatalities also tend to result in more injuries. I removed observations with missing fatality or injury counts and created a scatter plot comparing the two variables. I also added a regression line and calculated the Pearson correlation coefficient to measure the strength and direction of their relationship.

The correlation coefficient was approximately 0.534, indicating a moderate positive relationship between fatalities and injuries. This suggests that terrorist incidents resulting in higher numbers of fatalities also tend to result in higher numbers of injuries. However, the relationship is not perfect, meaning that some incidents result in many injuries but relatively few fatalities, while others result in more fatalities than injuries. These findings demonstrate that the severity of terrorist attacks can vary considerably across incidents.

## Conclusion 
This project analyzed global terrorism trends between 1970 and 2017, focusing on attack frequency, geographic distribution, attack methods, and severity. The results showed that terrorist attacks increased significantly over time, peaking at 16,903 incidents in 2014. Iraq recorded the most attacks, followed by Pakistan and Afghanistan, while hijackings had the highest average fatalities per incident. The Middle East and North Africa and South Asia experienced the greatest concentrations of terrorist activity, particularly during the 2010s. Additionally, fatalities and injuries showed a moderate positive correlation.

Overall, these findings highlight how terrorist activity varies across time, location, and attack type. This analysis provides valuable insights into historical security threats and patterns that could support national security research. However, because the dataset ends in 2017, future research should incorporate more recent data to examine current terrorism trends.
